scenes.tts: Every spike ends with potassium leaving the neuron. Where does all that potassium go?
scenes.visual: A single spike trace on a dark field; on its falling phase, small purple K+ dots stream out of a neuron outline. The question appears beside it.
scenes.narration: Every spike ends with potassium leaving the neuron. Where does all that potassium go?

scenes.tts: Into the gaps between brain cells. Those gaps are narrow. Together they are only about a fifth of the tissue.
scenes.visual: A block of grey matter zooms down to tightly packed cells. The extracellular space is drawn as thin bright channels between them. Label: about one fifth of the volume. Scale note: gaps tens of nanometres wide.
scenes.narration: Into the gaps between brain cells. Those gaps are narrow. Together they are only about a fifth of the tissue.

scenes.tts: Inside a neuron, potassium is high. Outside, it is low.
scenes.visual: Two concentration bars side by side: inside 140 mM (tall), outside 3 mM (short).
scenes.narration: Inside a neuron, potassium is high. Outside, it is low.

scenes.tts: A burst of firing lets some potassium out. Which concentration changes more, inside or outside? And which change matters more for the voltage?
scenes.visual: On screen: Pause. Which bar changes more? Which change matters more for the voltage?
scenes.narration: A burst of firing lets some potassium out. Which concentration changes more, inside or outside? And which change matters more for the voltage?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: In proportion, the outside, by a wide margin. Take a simple model: the space outside is a fifth of the tissue, and the firing neurons fill a third of the space inside.
scenes.visual: A burst of spikes. K+ dots leave the neuron. Volume blocks: outside 0.20 of the tissue; inside 0.80, with the firing neurons shaded as one third of it (0.80/3). On screen only: illustrative fixed, well-mixed pools; Vi/Vo = 1.33.
scenes.narration: In proportion, the outside, by a wide margin. Take a simple model: the space outside is a fifth of the tissue, and the firing neurons fill a third of the space inside.

scenes.tts: Then the same potassium changes the outside concentration about one and a third times as much as the inside one.
scenes.visual: The conserved transfer animates: the outside bar climbs by 1 mM while the shaded inside pool drops by 0.75 mM. On screen only: same ions, +1 mM outside, −0.75 mM in the firing neurons.
scenes.narration: Then the same potassium changes the outside concentration about one and a third times as much as the inside one.

scenes.tts: And the outside starts low. One extra millimolar raises it by a third. Losing three quarters of one inside changes it by about half a percent.
scenes.caption: And the outside starts low. One extra mM raises it by a third. Losing 0.75 mM inside changes it by about half a percent.
scenes.visual: On screen only, labelled 'the same transfer': 3 → 4 mM outside = +33%; 140 → 139.25 mM inside = −0.5%.
scenes.narration: And the outside starts low. One extra mM raises it by a third. Losing 0.75 mM inside changes it by about half a percent.

scenes.tts: Potassium's equilibrium potential, E K, depends on the ratio of outside to inside. In this model, the outside change moves it about sixty times as much as the inside change.
scenes.caption: Potassium's equilibrium potential, E_K, depends on the ratio of outside to inside. In this model, the outside change moves it about 60 times as much as the inside change.
scenes.visual: Formula card: at 37 °C, E_K = 61.5 mV × log10([K+]o / [K+]i). Both terms stay visible; the [K+]o term glows. Label: outside contribution dominates in this model (140/3 × 1.33 ≈ 62).
scenes.narration: Potassium's equilibrium potential, E_K, depends on the ratio of outside to inside. In this model, the outside change moves it about 60 times as much as the inside change.

scenes.tts: In cat cortex, strong repetitive stimulation raised outside potassium to a ceiling of about ten millimolar.
scenes.caption: In cat cortex, strong repetitive stimulation raised outside potassium to a ceiling of about 10 mM.
scenes.visual: The outside bar rises from 3 to 10 mM and a dashed ceiling line appears at 10 mM: measured ceiling, cat cortex. Ordinary activity: far below.
scenes.narration: In cat cortex, strong repetitive stimulation raised outside potassium to a ceiling of about 10 mM.

scenes.tts: At that ceiling, E K sits about thirty-two millivolts more positive than at rest.
scenes.caption: At that ceiling, E_K sits about 32 mV more positive than at rest.
scenes.visual: A voltage scale from E_K to E_Na, as in the action-potential films. The E_K marker swings right from −102.6 mV to −70.5 mV. On screen only: [K+]i held at 140 mM; 61.5 × log10(3/140) = −102.6; 61.5 × log10(10/140) = −70.5; shift +32 mV.
scenes.narration: At that ceiling, E_K sits about 32 mV more positive than at rest.

scenes.tts: Does the neuron's resting potential move that far too?
scenes.visual: A second marker, labelled resting potential, sits beside the E_K marker. On screen: Pause. Does it move 32 mV?
scenes.narration: Does the neuron's resting potential move that far too?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Less far, but the same way. In a simple model, it moves about half as far.
scenes.visual: The resting-potential marker slides right about half the distance the E_K marker moved. On screen only: about 16 mV (10 to 21 mV in simple models).
scenes.narration: Less far, but the same way. In a simple model, it moves about half as far.

scenes.tts: A resting neuron is mostly, but not only, permeable to potassium. Sodium pulls on its voltage too.
scenes.visual: A thick purple rope pulls the resting marker toward E_K; a thin orange rope pulls it toward E_Na.
scenes.narration: A resting neuron is mostly, but not only, permeable to potassium. Sodium pulls on its voltage too.

scenes.tts: A modest rise brings the neuron closer to threshold, so it fires more easily. More firing releases more potassium.
scenes.visual: A threshold line on the scale; the resting marker edges toward it. A circular arrow: more firing → more K+ outside → closer to threshold.
scenes.narration: A modest rise brings the neuron closer to threshold, so it fires more easily. More firing releases more potassium.

scenes.tts: That loop can feed a seizure.
scenes.visual: The circular arrow speeds up and glows red. Label: a loop that can feed a seizure.
scenes.narration: That loop can feed a seizure.

scenes.tts: A large, sustained rise can do the opposite. Sodium channels inactivate, and the neuron can stop firing.
scenes.visual: The marker held far to the right; sodium channel icons shut one by one; the spike train goes flat. Label: depolarization block.
scenes.narration: A large, sustained rise can do the opposite. Sodium channels inactivate, and the neuron can stop firing.

scenes.tts: So here is the rule. Small space outside, big change outside.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card, title: Small space outside, big change outside.
scenes.narration: So here is the rule. Small space outside, big change outside.

scenes.tts: A little released potassium is a big change outside, in proportion, and a tiny one inside. So in models like this one, E K's shift comes mostly from outside.
scenes.caption: A little released potassium is a big change outside, in proportion, and a tiny one inside. So in models like this one, E_K's shift comes mostly from outside.
scenes.visual: The card adds: K+ released by firing is a big proportional change in [K+]o and a tiny one in [K+]i, so in this model the shift in E_K comes mostly from outside.
scenes.narration: A little released potassium is a big change outside, in proportion, and a tiny one inside. So in models like this one, E_K's shift comes mostly from outside.

scenes.tts: So a neuron's resting potential depends on cells that keep clearing that space.
scenes.visual: The card adds: so the resting potential depends on cells that keep clearing that space. Astrocyte outlines fade in around the neuron.
scenes.narration: So a neuron's resting potential depends on cells that keep clearing that space.
